h2: What a UT Level 2 online course covers
html:
A UT Level 2 online course is for technicians who already hold, or are close to, UT Level I and need the formal Level II training hours their written practice requires. The online part carries the theory; the practical skills are built and examined on real equipment. This page covers the online course itself. The full Level II route, including experience hours and examinations, is on UT Level 2 training.

Theory covered online

  • Sound-beam physics for ultrasonic testing Level II work: beam spread, near field, attenuation and mode conversion.
  • Angle-beam examination with shear wave probes: refracted angle, skip distance and surface distance, and plotting indications on a weld cross-section.
  • Calibration: distance-amplitude correction (DAC) and time-corrected gain (TCG), reference reflectors and transfer correction.
  • Flaw sizing by amplitude-drop methods and their limits, and when sizing passes to PAUT or TOFD.
  • Codes and acceptance: ASME Section V Articles 4 and 5, ASME B31.3 and AWS D1.1 acceptance criteria, and how to write a report a Level III will sign.
  • Writing a technique sheet from a procedure, a Level II responsibility under SNT-TC-1A.

What cannot be done online

The Level II practical examination asks you to calibrate, scan a weld specimen containing hidden flaws, find, size and evaluate them against acceptance criteria, and report the result. That needs a flaw detector, probes and test pieces. Trainees practise set-ups in the Practical NDT simulator and complete hands-on training and the practical at their employer's site.

Experience hours still count

Course hours are only one part of Level II. SNT-TC-1A also recommends documented experience in the method, and many employers expect most of it to be weld examination under a Level II or Level III before they will certify. Keep a log of the jobs, the hours and the supervisor from the start, because the Level III signing your certification will ask for it.

Who should take it

The course suits working UT Level I technicians who need Level II for weld work, technicians certified in other methods who are adding UT, and employers moving staff up a level without taking them off the job. If you are new to UT, start with the UT Level 1 course. For exam-style questions, try the UT practice tests, and for the next step after Level II weld work, see PAUT Level 2 training. To enrol, contact the training team.
